title.narrative: Improving access to basic life-saving quality health care and essential GBV services to affected IDPs, returnees, people in extremely-hard-to reach areas in Bama, Monguno and Bursari LGAs.

description.narrative:
ltpgtltpgtAccording to the WHO, in 2022, cholera outbreaks were caused by a lack of access to healthcare and occurred in more than 30 states, with at least 15,000 cases being reported in the north-east and more than 460 fatalities in Nigeria. Millions of people, mostly from isolated rural agricultural settlements, have been forced by insecurity to flee their homes in search of safety in urban communities, which limits women's access to the few services available and raises the risk of women dying during pregnancy, childbirth, and postpartum. It has changed the dynamics within households, made poor living conditions worse, and made women and girls more vulnerable to domestic violence, forced marriage, sexual exploitation, human trafficking, abuse, and neglect.lt/pgt
ltpgtThe project will make sure that affected IDPs, returnees, residents of remote locations, and host populations in Borno (Bama and Mongunu LGAs) and Yobe (Bursari LGAs), receive basic life-saving quality health care and GBV protection services, attendant will be hired and trained to support reproductive health services, safe and clean deliveries at the chosen LGA locations, and support for exclusive breastfeeding in Danari Lawanti (1) Turban Gida PHCC (b) Guji Matalari Ward (2) Ajiri PHCC (c) Julluri Damnawa Ward (3) Julluri PHCC (d) Kaliyari Ward (4) Kurnawa PHCC (f) Masaba Ward and (5) Masaba PHCC) of Bursari LGA of Yobe state.lt/pgt
ltpgtPriority will be given to vital life-saving GBV mitigation services, MHPSS, and GBV case management, which will include providing GBV survivors with quality health care, establish OSC in Bama to provide psychosocial support referral strengthening, legal support, security and safety, economic empowerment, provision of dignity and clean, safe delivery kits and other supplies, and strengthening local institutions and systems. Additionally, it would look into GBV cases, maintain confidentiality, run extensive awareness campaigns for GBV, PSEA, and SRH, and teach men and boys how to work as allies in Monguno LGA and strengthens the WGSS in Bama LGA.lt/pgt
ltpgtRHHF will use the proposed 6-month project to accomplish the following by doing the following: creating three mobile outreach health teams made up of trained CHEWs, JCHEWs, and CHVs to serve the preselected communities, allocating trained health workers to the supporting facilities in accordance with the SMoH standard, and improving the capacity of the health workers (CHEWs, JCHEWs, TBAs, and CHVs) to be involved in providing basic life-saving quality health care services to conflict-affected individuals who are facing food insecurity and nutrition crisis challenges.lt/pgt
ltpgtBasic antenatal and postpartum care will be provided by licensed midwives, and community health volunteers will receive training in risk communication and community engagement. To assist five (5) healthcare facilities and three (3) mobile outreach teams in delivering integrated primary health care services, necessary medications, pharmaceuticals, and consumables will be made available. Additionally, the project will help the SPHCDA by offering emergency integrated primary health care services, such as the treatment of common illnesses, antenatal care, safe delivery, referral services in IDP camps and host communities to medical facilities, and services for waterborne illnesses.lt/pgt
ltpgtBuilding the capacity of the health workers to be engaged in other to provide basic life-saving quality health care services to conflict-affected individuals who are facing food insecurity and nutrition crisis challenges, formulating three mobile outreach health teams that will consist of trained CHEW, are just a few of the goals that the proposed project is intended to achieve in accordance with the Reserve Allocation Paper and the sector-specific priorities. Additionally, trained traditional birth attendants will be employed to support reproductive health services and secure deliveries.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtlt/pgtlt/pgt
